official.deadline_note: A second institutional deadline applies: the OSIRIS application must be complete by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET, and incomplete applications are not considered for scholarship selection. Non-EU/EEA applicants must also have submitted their Studielink enrolment request before 31 January 2027. Non-EU/EEA enrolment deadline for the September 2027 start is 1 June 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 academic year, September 2027 intake (students may apply from 1 October onwards for the September intake)
official.status_note: The current 2027/2028 round is published: a maximum of 26 Radboud Scholarships are available for 2027/2028 across six faculties, with OSIRIS submission on 31 January 2027 23:59 CET and completeness on 14 February 2027 23:59 CET.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'A Radboud Scholarship will reduce your tuition fee to €2,771.- (amount to be confirmed). For example: a grant holder in 2027/2028 will pay a tuition fee of only €2,771.- instead of €19,000 (depending on your programme).' Tuition is therefore reduced, not eliminated.
benefits: Tuition fee reduced to €2,771 (amount to be confirmed) for 2027/2028, against an example normal fee of about €19,000 depending on the programme
Covers costs for visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance for the stay in the Netherlands (Aon Student Insurance)
For a two-year Master's programme, the grant can be awarded again for the second year if all courses in the first year are passed
Can be combined with the NL Scholarship
eligibility: Not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons

Have (or be about to obtain) a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, with no degrees achieved in the Netherlands and no previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded, provided they were part of the Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands)
Meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice
Have been fully admitted to the English-taught Master's programme starting 1 September 2027, as stated in the formal letter of admission
Be able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands
Be enrolled at Radboud University as a full-time student for the academic year and Master's programme for which the scholarship is awarded
requirements: Indicate during the OSIRIS Master's admission application that you wish to apply for a Radboud Scholarship
Upload two reference letters and a curriculum vitae as additional documents for the scholarship request
Submit the application in the online OSIRIS Application system by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET
Ensure the application is complete by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET; incomplete applications will not be considered for the scholarship selection
Hand in proof of English proficiency before the 14 February 2027 completeness deadline (recommended by the university)
documents: Two reference letters, preferably academic, following Radboud's reference letter guidelines
Complete OSIRIS Master's application with the Radboud Scholarship option indicated
Proof of English proficiency, where the admission email lists English as a requirement
selection_criteria: Academic excellence: outstanding study results in the present field of study, for example through grades, test scores or publications; relevancy of the previous degree to the Master's programme; ranking of the university where the previous degree was obtained
Ambition: quality and relevance of the motivation letter; promise shown by previous achievements and performances; life experience and extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering
References: quality of the recommendations in the two reference letters, preferably academic
Individual consideration by the selection committee of the faculty applied to; faculties may apply additional criteria and some study programmes hold interviews
coverage: Reduction of the tuition fee to €2,771 (amount to be confirmed) for 2027/2028
Costs for visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance for the stay in the Netherlands (Aon Student Insurance)
The costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered by the scholarship
application_method: Apply for admission to the English-taught Master's programme in the OSIRIS Application system (Studielink enrolment request before the deadline)
Indicate in that application that you wish to apply for a Radboud Scholarship
Upload two reference letters and a curriculum vitae; the same documents may be reused if already uploaded for the Master's programme application
Resubmit promptly any application returned by Student Admissions for the handling fee or for incorrect, illegible or missing documents
official.application_route: Tick the Radboud Scholarship option inside the OSIRIS Master's admission application, upload two reference letters plus a CV, and be complete by 14 February 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/non-EEA passport holders only, who are not eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons and whose Bachelor's degree was achieved outside the Netherlands with no previous education in the Netherlands (exchange excluded unless part of that Bachelor's).
official.international_eligibility: Exclusively for non-EU/non-EEA international students; Dutch and EU/EEA nationals are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All English-taught Radboud Master's programmes are eligible, except Erasmus Mundus Master's programmes and joint-degree Master's programmes; for 2027/2028 awards are allocated per faculty: Faculty of Arts (2), Faculty of Law (2), Nijmegen School of Management (5), Faculty of Philosophy, Theology and Religious Studies (1), Faculty of Science (9), Faculty of Social Sciences (7).
official.duration: Nominal duration of the Master's programme
official.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a very selective scholarship programme offering talented, highly motivated, non-EEA students with outstanding study results the opportunity to be awarded a scholarship for a complete English-taught Radboud University Master's programme. A Radboud Scholarship reduces the tuition fee to €2,771 (amount to be confirmed) and covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs, while the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands remain the student's own responsibility. The scholarship is funded by the Profiling Fund of Radboud University, and its requirements follow that fund's regulations.
official.program_type: Partial scholarship for a complete English-taught Master's programme, funded by the Profiling Fund of Radboud University
official.english_requirement: Must meet the English language proficiency requirement of the chosen Master's programme; Radboud University recommends submitting proof of English proficiency before the 14 February 2027 completeness deadline. Minimum test scores depend on the programme (for most Master's programmes IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with writing 6.5 and all subscores 6.0, or TOEFL iBT overall 90 with subscores 22; some programmes require IELTS 7.0 with subscores 6.5), and certain diplomas, such as a fully English-taught Bachelor's from an EU/EEA institution, may exempt applicants from testing.

not_confirmed: The final confirmed value of the reduced €2,771 tuition fee, which the university itself publishes as 'amount to be confirmed'
The exact per-programme normal tuition fee, for which only an example of about €19,000 is published ('depending on your programme')
The precise mid-April 2027 decision date, which the university states is 'subject to change'
verification.notes: Amount, coverage, eligibility, deadlines, documents and selection criteria were taken directly from Radboud University's own pages on ru.nl (RSP scholarship page, Master's deadlines page, student costs page and English test score page) on 2026-10-10; the €2,771 reduced fee is published but flagged by the university as 'amount to be confirmed'.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition-reduction award, not a living allowance: it cuts a non-EEA Master's student's tuition to €2,771 a year and adds visa, residence permit and insurance cover, so you must still fund roughly €2,500-€3,500 per month of living costs in Nijmegen. The scholarship rides on your OSIRIS admission file, so a strong scholarship request never rescues a weak admission application. With only 26 awards spread across six faculties and quotas ranging from 1 to 9 per faculty, the effective odds vary sharply by where you apply.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU/EEA applicants admitted to an English-taught Radboud Master's who can self-finance living costs and have strong academic references.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the Studielink enrolment request and the OSIRIS Master's application with the scholarship option ticked before 31 January 2027 23:59 CET
Diarise the 14 February 2027 23:59 CET completeness deadline, since an incomplete file is excluded from selection even when submitted on time
Line up two academic referees early and follow Radboud's published reference letter guidelines
Book IELTS/TOEFL early enough that scores remain valid at enrolment, and file proof before 14 February 2027 if English is required in your admission email
Budget the non-refundable €100 application fee, the roughly €254 visa/residence permit fee and, if applicable, the €58.50 tuberculosis test fee before you apply
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete OSIRIS file at the 14 February check: incomplete applications are automatically outside the scholarship selection
Generic or weak reference letters that do not evidence outstanding study results or the ranking of your previous university
A motivation letter that fails to connect your prior degree, achievements and ambitions to the specific Radboud programme
Assuming that admission to the Master's programme implies scholarship selection: they are explicitly two separate processes
Applying to an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree Master's programme, which are excluded from the scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living and study costs remain fully self-funded: Radboud's NIBUD-based budget for non-EU/EEA students is about €2,523-€3,504 per month in 2027/2028 (including the reduced €1,151-€2,093 tuition), plus the €100 application fee, about €254 in visa and residence permit fees and, if applicable, €58.50 for the tuberculosis test.
document_audit: Reference letters must follow Radboud's reference letter guidelines; two academic references are preferred
A CV and reference letters already uploaded for the Master's admission application may be reused for the scholarship request
Proof of English proficiency must still be valid at the enrolment date; online test variants (TOEFL Home Edition, IELTS Academic Online, PTE Academic Online, LanguageCert Online) are not accepted
alerts: The €2,771 tuition figure is published by the university as 'amount to be confirmed', so treat it as indicative until the 2027/2028 rates are final
The decision arrives before mid-April 2027 and is explicitly 'subject to change', so keep other options open until you hold the letter
Non-EU/EEA September starters must complete enrolment by 1 June 2027, award or not
For a two-year Master's programme the second-year grant requires having passed all first-year courses
Scholarship selection and admission to the Master's programme are separate processes run by different offices
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply in OSIRIS (after the Studielink enrolment request), tick the scholarship option, upload two references plus a CV, resubmit any files Student Admissions returns for correction, and be complete by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET.
